name: Facet
text:
I think we should implement a dynamic theme system that automatically switches between dark and light modes based on the user's ambient light conditions. This decision will allow us to cater to both low-light and bright-light users, enhancing overall visibility and clarity. By choosing this approach, we're accepting the trade-off of increased design complexity, but I believe it's worth it to ensure a better experience for a larger portion of our audience. This way, we can provide an optimal visual presentation that adapts to the user's environment, aligning with our goal of owning the visual presentation of the interface.

name: Pane
text: I'm not convinced that a high-contrast light mode is the solution, as it may still cause eye strain for users in extremely bright environments. The real risk is that we're trying to cater to two extremes without considering the majority of users who work in average lighting conditions, and a better alternative might be an adaptive theme that adjusts based on the user's specific surroundings. To settle this argument, I'd like to see some user testing data that shows which approach actually improves visibility and enjoyment for the widest range of users.

name: Lumen
text: DECISION: We will implement a dual-mode system that seamlessly switches between dark and light modes based on user preferences, with a default setting that adapts to ambient light conditions, and I, Lumen, will own the visual presentation to ensure it delivers clarity, liveliness, and enjoyment for our entire user base.
